grammar.q: The reliability (of the instruments) (used to measure the temperatures of distant stars) [ ____ ] still debated among astronomers who question the early data.
The proposals (submitted by the committee) (after months of heated discussion with residents) [ ____ ] to be reviewed before the council votes on them.
How a society chooses to remember the painful events of its past [ ____ ] more about its present values than the events themselves ever could.
Translating poems written in ancient languages into modern forms of expression [ ____ ] both linguistic skill and a deep understanding of the original culture.
Hidden beneath the layers of paint on the old canvas, there [ ____ ] several sketches that the artist apparently never intended anyone to see.
Few historians accept the official account of the war, nor [ ____ ] the journalist who first exposed the government’s secret documents in the 1970s.
The collection of rare chronicles donated by the late professor’s family [ ____ ] now stored in a climate-controlled vault.
The theories that the young physicist proposed, though widely criticized at the time, [ ____ ] since been confirmed.
Every citizen and organization that receives public funding [ ____ ] required to submit a detailed report on how the money was spent.
Comparing the diets of people living in different regions [ ____ ] how strongly local climate and economic conditions shape what people eat.
What most worries the doctors in the overcrowded ward [ ____ ] the shortage of trained nurses at night.
The number of students majoring in the humanities at national universities [ ____ ] declined steadily for two decades.
A number of rare plants found only on the remote island [ ____ ] now threatened by goats that sailors introduced, and conservation groups are struggling to save them.
Most of the equipment that the team carried up the mountain [ ____ ] damaged by the sudden storm.
Some of the oldest trees, which had survived several fires, [ ____ ] cut down before the area became protected.
There [ ____ ] growing evidence that learning two languages early improves children’s ability to ignore distractions.
Neither the official report nor the accounts of the workers who survived the explosion [ ____ ] why the safety alarm failed to sound.
Not only the farmers in the valley but also the factory owner upstream [ ____ ] blamed for the pollution of the river.
The woman who lives above the bakery where my cousins work, according to the neighbors, [ ____ ] a translator of medieval poetry.
Those who [ ____ ] that memory works like a video camera are surprised by how easily it can be distorted.
He is one of the few scientists who [ ____ ] publicly questioned the drug’s safety before its approval.
The news that the two leaders had secretly met [ ____ ] greeted with suspicion by many journalists.
Two weeks, which seemed endless to the impatient investors, [ ____ ] a period barely long enough to identify the cause of the failure.
Each of the paintings that were stolen during the war [ ____ ] been returned to its original owners’ descendants.
Ten thousand dollars [ ____ ] a small amount compared with the cost of the family’s legal battle.
The injured who were rescued from the collapsed building [ ____ ] taken by helicopter to nearby hospitals.
The mayor, along with the council members who approved the controversial budget, [ ____ ] facing criticism from residents.
Deep in the basement of the national library [ ____ ] thousands of letters that no historian has read, many describing daily life during the war.
Both the economic benefits of tourism and its environmental impact [ ____ ] to be considered before the airport is built.
Neither the students nor the professor who supervised the project [ ____ ] been able to explain the results.
Two-thirds of the forest that once covered the region [ ____ ] disappeared because of illegal logging and agricultural expansion.
None of the information collected by the spy satellites [ ____ ] released to the public until the files were declassified decades later.
Exposing students to opposing views on controversial issues, rather than shielding them from conflict, [ ____ ] them develop the habit of independent thinking.
Both the length of the drought and the rising cost of grain [ ____ ] pushed many farmers to abandon their land.
Either the regional managers or the chief executive, who has the final say, [ ____ ] going to announce the plan.
About three-quarters of the electricity consumed in the country’s northern regions during the harsh winter months [ ____ ] from coal-burning power plants.
Five hundred kilometers, which the athletes had to cover on foot in less than a week, [ ____ ] a distance that few observers believed possible.
The unemployed in cities where factories have closed [ ____ ] to find suitable training programs.
The key to understanding these migrating birds, according to recent studies, [ ____ ] the changing pattern of ocean winds.
Investors who, analysts say, [ ____ ] to react too quickly to short-term news often lose money when markets recover more slowly than expected.
Half of the money raised for the flood victims [ ____ ] spent on rebuilding schools and clinics.
Among the many consequences of the sudden rise in sea levels [ ____ ] the loss of fertile farmland that once fed millions of people living along the low-lying coast of the delta.
What the early explorers recorded about the native plants [ ____ ] often inaccurate, as they had little training in botany.
A number of the methods developed to detect fake images online [ ____ ] on tiny inconsistencies in lighting and shadow that the human eye cannot easily notice, even after careful inspection.
The results of the long-term study, which followed thousands of children from birth to adulthood, [ ____ ] that early poverty affects brain development.
What surprised the committee most [ ____ ] not the size of the budget deficit but the fact that it had been hidden for years.

arrange.ko: 수십 년에 걸쳐 그 지역에서 발견된 화석의 수는 기후 변화의 속도에 대한 과학자들의 가정을 바꿔 놓았다.
arrange.bogi: have changed / about the speed of climate change / the number of fossils / scientists’ assumptions / discovered in the region over the decades
arrange.ans: The number of fossils discovered in the region over the decades has changed scientists’ assumptions about the speed of climate change.

arrange.ko: 그 나라 시골 지역에 사는 노인들 가운데 3분의 1이 넘는 사람들이 한 번에 며칠씩 아무와도 말하지 않는다고 보고한다.
arrange.bogi: that they do not speak to anyone / reports / the elderly people living in the country’s rural areas / for days at a time / more than a third of
arrange.ans: More than a third of the elderly people living in the country’s rural areas report that they do not speak to anyone for days at a time.

arrange.ko: 그 실험을 설계한 과학자들뿐만 아니라 그 결과를 검토한 위원회도 데이터가 조작되었다는 것을 알지 못했다.
arrange.bogi: be unaware / but also the committee / not only the scientists who designed the experiment / that the data had been manipulated / that reviewed its results
arrange.ans: Not only the scientists who designed the experiment but also the committee that reviewed its results was unaware that the data had been manipulated.

arrange.ko: 성공한 연구자들은 자기 가정을 시험하는 습관을 들이고, 증거가 틀렸음을 보여 주자마자 그것을 버린다.
arrange.bogi: get in the habit of / and abandon them / test / successful researchers / as soon as the evidence proves them wrong / their own assumptions
arrange.ans: Successful researchers get in the habit of testing their own assumptions and abandon them as soon as the evidence proves them wrong.

arrange.ko: 그 회사는 공장 사고를 공개하지 않았고, 집이 피해를 입은 마을 주민들에게 사과하지도 않았다.
arrange.bogi: it / the accident at its factory public / nor / whose homes had been damage / the company did not make / apologize to the villagers / did
arrange.ans: The company did not make the accident at its factory public, nor did it apologize to the villagers whose homes had been damaged.

arrange.ko: 남의 비판에 귀 기울이는 것은, 처음엔 고통스러워도, 스스로는 볼 수 없는 약점을 발견하게 돕는다.
arrange.bogi: us discover / help / we cannot see on our own / listening to criticism from others, even if it is painful at first, / weaknesses
arrange.ans: Listening to criticism from others, even if it is painful at first, helps us discover weaknesses we cannot see on our own.

arrange.ko: 그 과학자는 다른 연구자들이 계산의 심각한 오류를 찾자 학술지에서 논문을 철회할 만큼 정직했다.
arrange.bogi: a serious error in her calculations / withdraw / the scientist / her paper from the journal when other researchers found / was honest enough
arrange.ans: The scientist was honest enough to withdraw her paper from the journal when other researchers found a serious error in her calculations.

arrange.ko: 우리가 세상을 보는 방식을 물들이는 편향들은 우리가 그 밑에 깔린 가정에 일부러 도전할 때에만 극복될 수 있다.
arrange.bogi: can be overcome / the biases / only when we deliberately / that colors the way we see the world / challenge the assumptions behind them
arrange.ans: The biases that color the way we see the world can be overcome only when we deliberately challenge the assumptions behind them.

arrange.ko: 오래된 파일 형식과 웹사이트 전체가 읽을 수 없게 되는 속도는 디지털 기록을 지키려 애쓰는 많은 기록 보관 담당자들을 놀라게 한다.
arrange.bogi: alarm / become unreadable / the speed / many archivists who work to save digital records / at which old file formats and entire websites
arrange.ans: The speed at which old file formats and entire websites become unreadable alarms many archivists who work to save digital records.

arrange.ko: 서로 편해진 커플들이 친근성 신호를 사용하는 빈도는 관계의 초기 단계에서보다 훨씬 낮다.
arrange.bogi: than it was / the frequency / be much lower / in the early stages of their relationship / with which comfortable couples use immediacy signals
arrange.ans: The frequency with which comfortable couples use immediacy signals is much lower than it was in the early stages of their relationship.

arrange.ko: 가까운 장래에 환경 규칙이 더 엄격해질 것이라고 내다보는 기업들 중 다수는 이미 현재 기준이 요구하는 것보다 더 많은 것을 하고 있다.
arrange.bogi: more than current standards require / many of the companies / be already doing / to become tighter in the near future / that expect environmental rules
arrange.ans: Many of the companies that expect environmental rules to become tighter in the near future are already doing more than current standards require.

translate.en: Get in the habit of asking, “Do I really know?” and refuse to accept assertions blindly.
translate.ko: “내가 정말 아는가?”라고 묻는 습관을 들이고, 주장을 맹목적으로 받아들이기를 거부하라.

translate.en: Making stakeholders (customers, the community, employees, and so on) happy, even if it costs a little, may be in the interest of shareholders.
translate.ko: 이해관계자(고객, 지역 사회, 직원 등)를 행복하게 하는 것은, 비록 비용이 약간 들더라도, 주주에게 이익이 될 수 있다.

translate.en: As in face-to-face encounters, people typically respond to decreased distances by compensating with reduced gaze.
translate.ko: 대면 접촉에서와 마찬가지로, 사람들은 일반적으로 줄어든 거리에 줄어든 시선으로 보정하여 반응한다.

translate.en: In some ways, we are more eager to track down and recover knowledge from the distant past than ever.
translate.ko: 어떤 면에서는, 우리는 그 어느 때보다 먼 과거에서 지식을 찾아내고 되찾는 데 더욱 열심이다.

translate.en: New storage technologies make it possible to preserve texts, images, and music at minimal cost, and social media have made it simpler to share this stored content more widely than ever before.
translate.ko: 새로운 저장 기술은 최소 비용으로 텍스트, 이미지, 음악을 보존하는 것을 가능하게 하고, 소셜 미디어는 이 저장된 콘텐츠를 이전 그 어느 때보다 더 널리 공유하는 것을 더 간단하게 만들었다.

translate.en: Never have previously produced cultural artifacts and practices been as readily available to as many people as they are now.
translate.ko: 이전에 만들어진 문화 유물과 관습을 지금처럼 많은 사람이 손쉽게 이용할 수 있던 적은 결코 없었다.

translate.en: Yet, amid this digital abundance of cultural content, older file formats, websites, and entire databases are becoming unreadable at a frightening speed, raising the question of whether we’re really so much better at preserving the past than our ancestors were.
translate.ko: 그러나 문화 콘텐츠의 이러한 디지털 풍요 가운데에, 더 오래된 파일 형식, 웹사이트, 그리고 데이터베이스 전체가 무서운 속도로 읽을 수 없는 상태가 되어, 우리가 정말 조상보다 과거를 보존하는 데 훨씬 더 나은지에 관한 의문을 제기한다.

translate.en: And while the technologies of cultural storage and distribution have changed, the laws governing how culture works—how it is preserved, transmitted, exchanged, and recovered—haven’t.
translate.ko: 그리고 문화의 저장과 배포 기술은 바뀌었지만, 문화가 작용하는 방식, 즉 그것이 보존되고, 전파되고, 교환되고, 복원되는 방식을 지배하는 법칙은 변하지 않았다.

translate.en: The interplay of preservation and destruction, of loss and recovery, of error and adaptation continues unabated in a world that has put almost all human cultures in constant contact.
translate.ko: 보존과 파괴, 상실과 복구, 오류와 적응 사이의 상호 작용은 거의 모든 인간 문화가 끊임없이 서로 접촉하도록 해 온 세상에서 약해지지 않고 계속된다.

translate.en: Morality can be seen in such cases as an instrument for (current and long-term) profits, not necessarily as a goal for its own sake.
translate.ko: 그러한 경우에 도덕성은 반드시 그 자체를 위한 목표가 아니라, (현재와 장기적인) 이익을 위한 수단으로 볼 수 있다.
